# Queuelet exploration protocol

An experiment teaches us about the inherited system by comparing a prediction with observation. Source reading is allowed and valuable; the register, proof scripts and SUT history are withheld. This document defines the local record and roles. It does not describe expected defects.

## Roles and export

The coordinator prepares a charter and an empty export directory. The seeder/fixer and explorer must be from different model families. Every experiment uses a fresh headless explorer. The reviewer independently checks the checkpoint and blindness boundary.

Export only the previous tag’s `books/explore-it/project`, `books/explore-it/exploration`, `books/explore-it/skills` and `books/explore-it/lessons`, preserving their relative paths. From the repository root, with the chosen tag and an existing empty destination:

```sh
git archive "$experiment_tag" books/explore-it/project books/explore-it/exploration books/explore-it/skills books/explore-it/lessons | tar -x -C "$export_dir"
```

The export has no `.git`, `PLAN.md`, `register/`, seeder proofs or hidden copy of repository history. Inspect its file list before dispatch. Existing experiment records, disclosed previous lessons and repro scripts may be present at later tags; they are prior knowledge, never a briefing about unfound targets. Keep the new charter and brief free of planted hints. The explorer can read any file in the export, including all source, and run the lab; it must not read outside the export or consult the originating checkout. Where external tools/services are necessary, their permitted use is specified in the brief rather than granting access to outside source or answer keys.

The committed `experiments/NN-<slug>/brief.md` names the export path, charter, relevant skill, this protocol, budget, permission profile and acceptance checks. It states the export-only reading rule and contains no information about what is planted. The coordinator supplies the charter; it is not assembled by the explorer from the plan.

## Before the probe

Each charter has one target, named resources/instruments and one kind of information:

```text
Explore <target> with <resources> to discover <information>.
I predict <observable behavior>.
Source: <spec line, code file:line, model cell, previous surprise or risk hypothesis>.
I would be wrong if <observable refutation>.
Budget: 60 minutes wall clock; planned reading / probing / writing split.
```

Write predictions and refutation conditions before executing the corresponding probe, including new hypotheses formed mid-run. A source reading is evidence for a prediction, not its confirmation. Separate should (named oracle), predicted (what code appears to do) and observed (what ran). Later observations can shape the next probe within this charter. Backlog adjacent questions as `#offcharter`; the explorer never widens the assignment.

The run budget includes reading, probing, resetting and writing. Track elapsed time and the actual reading/probing/writing split. No probe is worth losing the record to a time-out.

## During the run

Keep `experiments/NN-<slug>/notes.md` as timestamped entries. Use UTC timestamps and these tags:

| Tag | Record |
|---|---|
| `#read` | Source observation with file:line and its interpretation |
| `#hypothesis` | Id, source, prediction and refutation before the probe |
| `#obs` | Exact command, trimmed output and observed effects |
| `#surprise` | A discrepancy requiring characterization |
| `#bug` | Evidence and report link for an oracle violation |
| `#question` | An unresolved question or missing observation |
| `#offcharter` | Adjacent lead saved without expanding the target |

Retain dead ends, failed commands and timestamps. Trim repetitive output but retain evidence that determines the judgment. Preserve raw output or a linked artifact when trimming would lose meaning. Record fixture/reset identity, actors and relevant clock state. Read-only database observations are permitted; inject failures through lab/partner controls, container actions or documented clock controls, not hidden service paths or ad hoc source changes.

When no console answers a question, record a testability request with the question, missing signal, minimal hook and validation probe. The explorer proposes hooks; the fixer implements them in the separate fix stage.

## Characterize surprises

Every `#surprise` ends in a defect report or an explicit written reason it is not one. Isolate variables and reduce the reproduction. If it will not reproduce, preserve exact original state, vary one thing at a time, suspect timing and clock sources, and keep attempts and uncertainty in the log.

Reports under `defects/` contain:

- Title and tag/build seen at; link to the original observation.
- Exact minimal setup and steps, including actor, clock and fixture assumptions.
- Expected behavior with its named oracle: spec line, Never/Always rule, comparable system/standard or approximation with bounds.
- Observed behavior and evidence.
- Variables isolated, including what did not matter.
- Sibling check: where else the same cause could live, with file:line, or “none found.” Predictions about siblings must precede their probes.
- Severity with impact, and status: `open`, `fixed in lesson NN`, `won't fix: <why>` or `spec`.

The explorer writes reports in its own words with local provisional identifiers if necessary. The coordinator reconciles them with the hidden register: retain the planted `D##` id when matched; assign `U##` to an unplanned finding. Identifier reconciliation must not insert the register’s explanation into the explorer’s account.

## Close and score the run

Write `revealed.md` with charter status (`done`, `needs more` or `blocked`), elapsed time and reading/probing/writing split, what the system showed in plain words, model delta with file/cell links, unresolved uncertainties and next hypotheses. End with this score table, using actual counts and evidence links:

| Measure | Count | Evidence / counting basis |
|---|---|---|
| Hypotheses stated | | Distinct ids stated before probing |
| Hypotheses confirmed | | Predictions supported by the stated observation |
| Hypotheses refuted | | Stated refutation condition observed |
| Code-reading predictions contradicted by the running system | | Refuted subset whose recorded source was code |
| Defects found | | Distinct evidenced reports, excluding disclosure |
| Model cells filled | | Previously unobserved cells now supported by evidence |

Record hypotheses left `needs more` explicitly; confirmed plus refuted need not equal stated. Neither running a command nor adding an inferred diagram cell establishes observed coverage. Count a repeated observation once, and link separate defect findings even when one probe exposes several. A prediction of a defect can be confirmed while the product behavior violates its oracle; keep these judgments separate.

An experiment may need a second run with a narrowed charter. It closes after at most two runs. The coordinator discloses remaining planted misses in the lesson note under “What the experiment missed, and why,” and the fixer flags them `disclosed`. Never backfill these into the explorer’s notes, scores or finds. Preserve out-of-order and unplanned discoveries as they happened.

## Backlog and living models

`hypotheses.md` retains every proposed hypothesis: id, statement/prediction, source, refutation, intended probe/experiment and status (`open` or `experiment NN: confirmed|refuted|needs more`). Keep original statements when updating outcomes.

Models under `models/` grow from observations: `map.md`, `nouns-verbs.md`, `variables.md`, `rules.md`, `entities.md`, `states.md`, `ecosystem.md` and, after evidence supports cause analysis, `causes.md`. Label inference and uncertainty. Later experiments revise earlier models; their diffs are evidence of learning. In a cause-prediction run, commit or timestamp the predicted-defects table before running the confirming probes.

## Handoff and verification

The coordinator commits experiment artifacts as produced, formatting only. Fixes belong in a separate fresh fixer run from the seeder’s family, using the reports as brief. The fixer changes only named findings, adds a regression check per defect under `project/test/checks/` and black-box repro scripts under `project/lab/repro/`, and writes the lesson note. A spec silence also needs a spec line and the coordinator’s one-line decision in the fix commit body. The lesson tag points at the fix commit. Fix history remains separate from the experiment record.

`make verify LESSON=NN` resets and runs that experiment’s repros and checks. Its final verdict is `FIXED AND CHECKED:` after repair or `DEFECTS REPRODUCED:` against the earlier version. Repros report `PRESENT:` or `ABSENT:` per defect; thresholds are binary and may not be weakened to hide a defect. `REF=<tag>` uses the current repros against earlier SUT code. `make checks` runs all regression checks; `make test` runs unit tests. `make dwell LESSON=NN` optionally shows present/absent across earlier tags; its result does not gate the verdict. Lesson 00 uses `BASELINE HOLDS:`.

Lesson notes include actual found/missed/found-early/unplanned outcomes, the score and before/after evidence. Review checks that previous-version repros still reproduce the finding, models match evidence and no answer key leaked into the brief or export.

## Source and local adaptations

Hendrickson, [*Explore It!*](https://pragprog.com/titles/ehxta/explore-it/) (2013): 1.1–1.3, 2.1–2.4 and 2.6, Chapter 3, 10.4, 11.5–11.6 and 13.3. Section numbering checked against the publisher’s contents extract; detailed text review remains pending. Blind exports, split agent roles, explicit prediction/refutation lines, score format and the two-commit lesson are this repo’s implementation of the approved plan, not claims of prescribed book formats.

## Status

**done.** The charter prediction "deleting an owner leaves orphans" was **refuted** for the owners the API lets you delete
(queue → jobs, queue → schedules): the lesson-01 fix added foreign keys (002.sql:9-17) and a locked 409 check, and
70 race rounds produced no orphan. It **holds** for one pair the schema never linked: job → attempts (E06-F07).
Following the data turned up more than deleting owners did. Seven reports in total.

## Elapsed

15:28:42Z → 15:48Z (stack stopped 15:47:26Z; STATE written after), about 20 minutes of the 60-minute budget.

| Activity | Minutes (approx.) | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Reading | 3 | 15:28:42–15:31:37: STATE, charter, brief, protocol, skill, SPEC, migrations, the API/jobs/schedule/webhook/worker/client source; the stack built in the background |

## What the system showed

- **Owners refuse rather than orphan.** A queue that has any job (even a cancelled one) or a schedule gets 409
  `queue_not_empty`. An empty queue gets 204, a missing or foreign one 404. Racing 16 enqueues against a DELETE never
  left an orphan. The writes that lose the race, though, are answered **400 invalid_job** (enqueue) or **500
  database_error** (schedule create), with the foreign-key constraint name in the message, instead of 404
  → [E06-F06](../../defects/E06-F06-enqueue-racing-queue-delete-400-fk-text.md).
- **Schedule DELETE always says 204.** It says 204 for an id that never existed, for one already deleted, and for
  another tenant's schedule (which is left alone). GET, PATCH and run of the same ids return 404
  → [E06-F01](../../defects/E06-F01-schedule-delete-missing-204.md).
- **The cron path creates jobs no other path allows.** A schedule's payload may be omitted, `null`, an array, a string
  or a number. `run` rejects these (400), but the cron fire stores them as job payloads. On `emails`, an array payload
  is a poison job for the documented worker: the worker can't decode the lease, never acks or nacks, and logs no job id.
  The job then burns 3 attempts by lease expiry and dies with "lease expired"
  → [E06-F02](../../defects/E06-F02-schedule-payload-not-validated.md).
- **Data journey (one payload through every hop).** The API, jsonb storage, lease bytes, ack, outbox and partner bytes
  keep `9007199254740993` and `1.10` exactly, and the signature is valid over the bytes sent. jsonb and Go's encoder
  normalise the form without changing any value (`1e2`→`100`, key order, last duplicate wins, `<` → `<`), so this is
  not a defect. The loss happens in queuelet's own clients:
  - the sample worker's `echo` returns `9007199254740992` / `1.1`, and that is what the partner is notified
    → [E06-F03](../../defects/E06-F03-sample-worker-echo-loses-precision.md);
  - `qctl enqueue --payload` **stores** the rounded number, and `qctl job get` displays rounded numbers
    → [E06-F04](../../defects/E06-F04-qctl-rounds-payload-numbers.md).
- **Values the store cannot hold turn into a lease error.** An ack result or nack error that contains U+0000 gets
  409 `state_conflict` with driver text, while the caller still holds a valid lease. Enqueue gets 400 for the same
  character → [E06-F05](../../defects/E06-F05-nul-in-result-or-error-409-conflict.md).
- **Job removal leaves attempts behind.** Purge, DELETE and retention remove the job, but its attempt rows (including
  worker error text) stay in psql forever, unreachable through the API. Delivered outbox rows also stay
  → [E06-F07](../../defects/E06-F07-attempts-outlive-their-job.md).
- **What held** (no new defect):
  - queue PATCH changes dependents exactly as specified: existing jobs keep `max_attempts`, while new and `run` jobs
    take the new value; a pending notification keeps its URL and secret (valid signature with the old secret); URL `""`
    creates no more rows;
  - a pending row for a deleted job in a deleted queue is still delivered;
  - deleting a worker counts the released attempt (lesson-05 fix, regression only);
  - job events stay readable through the API and the API log after purge, delete and retention, and those two paths
    agree with psql;
  - the background loop logged no error during any probe.
- **Surprises that are not defects** (reasons in the notes' surprise ledger):
  - jsonb/HTML normalisation;
  - a retention change applies to jobs that are already terminal (SPEC has no snapshot rule);
  - an idempotency key is free again once its job is deleted;
  - the sample worker becomes a zombie after its row is deleted: it polls with 404 every second, never exits or
    re-registers, and the stranded job waits until someone restarts the container. SPEC states no client obligation
    here (Q-E06-1).

# Queuelet service contract

Queuelet stores jobs durably in PostgreSQL and distributes them to workers.
A namespace contains queues, workers and schedules. A bearer API key selects a
namespace; an administrative key may inspect namespace statistics.

## Authentication and responses

Every `/v1/` request requires `Authorization: Bearer <key>`.
A namespace key accesses only its namespace's resources.
The health and metrics endpoints are public.
JSON commands use `Content-Type: application/json`.
Errors have the form `{"error":{"code":"…","message":"…"}}` and a 4xx or 5xx
HTTP status. Successful reads and mutations return 200 unless stated otherwise.
Creation returns 201. Deletion returns 204. A missing resource returns 404.
A command incompatible with the current state returns 409.
A path no route serves is 404 and a method a route does not accept is 405, both
in the same error form.
Unknown fields and invalid enum values should be rejected as invalid commands.
A command body is exactly one JSON object in UTF-8. Trailing data, invalid UTF-8
and member names that match a documented field only when case is ignored are
rejected with 400 `invalid_json`.
Every seconds-valued field and `max_attempts` accepts at most 2147483647.
A `delay_seconds` (enqueue or nack) is never negative; a negative value is 400.

## Queues

`POST /v1/queues` creates a queue with a unique name within the namespace.
Names use 1–128 ASCII letters, digits, underscores and hyphens. Only a taken name
is a 409 conflict; an invalid or out-of-range setting is 400.
Configuration defaults are `lease_seconds:30`, `max_attempts:3`,
`backoff:{kind:"exponential",base_seconds:5}`, `retention_hours:24`.
Lease duration and maximum attempts must be positive; retention hours range from
0 through 1000000.
Backoff kind is `linear` or `exponential`; the base is a nonnegative number
of seconds. Failed jobs retry with exponential backoff from `base_seconds`
or linear backoff when configured. An optional `backoff.max_seconds`, at least
`base_seconds`, caps each wait. Without it each wait is capped at 3600 seconds,
or at `base_seconds` when that is larger. A computed wait never overflows: it is capped
at 2147483647 seconds, so a retry is never scheduled before the failure.
An optional `webhook:{url,secret}` receives terminal notifications.

`GET /v1/queues` lists the namespace's queues.
`GET /v1/queues/{name}` reads configuration.
`PATCH /v1/queues/{name}` updates lease duration, maximum attempts, retention
or webhook settings. Existing jobs retain their maximum-attempt setting.
Omitted members keep their value, inside `webhook` as well: a secret-only PATCH
keeps the URL and a URL-only PATCH keeps the secret.
`DELETE /v1/queues/{name}` removes a queue; owned jobs and schedules must not
become orphaned. Callers must handle a conflict for a nonempty queue.
`POST /v1/queues/{name}/pause` prevents new leases and scheduled deliveries.
`POST /v1/queues/{name}/resume` allows work again. Missed periodic ticks should
not create an unbounded burst of catch-up jobs.
`POST /v1/queues/{name}/purge` removes all pending jobs: scheduled, queued and retry_wait.
A job leased when its queue is purged keeps its lease: an ack completes it, and a
nack, lease expiry or worker deletion makes it `dead`, never pending again.

## Jobs

`POST /v1/queues/{name}/jobs` accepts `kind`, a JSON object `payload`, and
optional `priority`, `delay_seconds`, `run_at`, `max_attempts`, `idempotency_key`.
Kind is required. Priority ranges from 0 through 9 and defaults to 5.
Payload values are delivered to workers without loss of numeric precision.
Choose either delay in seconds or an RFC3339 `run_at`, never both.
A job due now is `queued`; a future job is `scheduled`.
The service promotes due jobs to `queued`.
A queue's maximum-attempt setting is copied to each new job unless overridden.
Repeated use of an idempotency key within a queue returns the original job.

`POST /v1/queues/{name}/jobs:batch` accepts `{"jobs":[…]}` with 1–500 jobs.
An empty or oversized batch is invalid and returns 400 without insertion.
A batch is atomic: an invalid element leaves none of its new jobs stored.
It returns `{"ids":[…]}` after accepted jobs are stored.
`GET /v1/queues/{name}/jobs` supports state, kind, limit and cursor filters.
The limit defaults to 100 and is at most 500. The returned next cursor can
be used to continue through increasing job ids.
Valid state filters are `scheduled`, `queued`, `leased`, `retry_wait`,
`succeeded`, `dead` and `cancelled`.
`GET /v1/jobs/{id}` returns the current job, payload, result and last error.
`GET /v1/jobs/{id}/attempts` returns completed attempts in numeric order.
Attempt `n` numbers every execution of the job and is never reused, across
operator retries too; the lease's `attempt` counts toward `max_attempts`.
`DELETE /v1/jobs/{id}` removes a terminal job.
Only a `leased` job has a lease token, holder and expiry; every exit from
`leased` clears all three; attempt rows keep the worker that ran them.

## Worker protocol

`POST /v1/workers` takes a name and an array of supported kinds.
It returns a worker id and token.
`DELETE /v1/workers/{id}` deregisters the worker and releases its active leases.
Each release records an unsuccessful attempt, as an expired lease does; a job
whose maximum attempts are exhausted becomes `dead` instead of `queued`.
`POST /v1/queues/{name}/lease` takes `worker_id` and `max_jobs` (1–100).
Only jobs with a kind supported by that worker are eligible.
Leasing is atomic; concurrent workers cannot acquire the same lease.
Higher priorities run first. Within a priority, jobs run FIFO by creation order.
The response includes job id, kind, payload, attempt, lease token and expiry.

A worker sends `POST /v1/jobs/{id}/heartbeat` with the lease token and positive
`extend_seconds` to extend its lease.
`POST /v1/jobs/{id}/ack` supplies the lease token and result and completes work.
`POST /v1/jobs/{id}/nack` supplies the lease token, an error and optional retry
boolean (default true) or a `delay_seconds` override.
Only the current lease holder may complete or extend a job. A lease ends at its
`lease_expires_at`: from that instant heartbeat, ack and nack are 409, whether or
not the background loop has released the job yet. There is no grace period.
Ack moves a leased job to `succeeded`.
Nack with retry moves a job to `retry_wait`; when due it becomes `queued`.
A failed job reaches `dead` when its maximum attempts are exhausted, or when
nacked with retry false. No job may execute more than its maximum attempts.
An expired lease records an unsuccessful attempt and releases the job for retry
unless the maximum attempts have been exhausted.

## Operator actions and retention

`POST /v1/jobs/{id}/cancel` cancels a nonterminal job.
A cancelled job is never run.
`POST /v1/jobs/{id}/retry` permits an operator to retry a dead job, resets its
attempt count and makes it immediately available.
Succeeded and cancelled jobs cannot be retried.
Terminal jobs are deleted after `retention_hours`.
The API returns complete stored results and errors.

## Schedules

`POST /v1/schedules` takes name, queue, kind, payload, cron, timezone and enabled.
Cron uses five fields: minute, hour, day of month, month and day of week.
Time zones use IANA identifiers, defaulting to UTC.
Schedule times follow the named zone's local civil time, including offset changes.
The enabled flag defaults to true; disabled schedules do not enqueue jobs.
`GET /v1/schedules` lists schedules; `GET /v1/schedules/{id}` reads one.
`PATCH /v1/schedules/{id}` updates cron, timezone or enabled status; the next fire
must reflect the current configuration.
`DELETE /v1/schedules/{id}` removes it.
`POST /v1/schedules/{id}/run` enqueues one immediate execution.

## Notifications and operations

Terminal transitions produce a webhook outbox entry when the queue has a URL.
The entry includes job id, state, result and last error.
Notification results preserve their JSON type; results and errors are complete.
Each POST carries `X-Queuelet-Signature`, a hex HMAC-SHA256 over the body using
the configured secret. Delivery is successful only on a 2xx response.
Failed notifications are retried. Delivery is at least once.

`GET /v1/queues/{name}/stats` and `GET /v1/namespaces/{name}/stats` expose counts
by exact state, oldest queued age in seconds and completed jobs in the last hour.
Queued age uses the later of creation and readiness, over queued rows only.
A job released by lease expiry or worker deletion becomes ready at the release.
`GET /health` returns service health; `GET /metrics` returns minimal text metrics.
The background loop promotes scheduled jobs, expires leases, fires cron schedules,
sweeps retention and delivers webhooks. It should recover after a database restart. Webhook latency must not block core
lifecycle progress. Health reports database availability and loop degradation;
an unavailable authentication store returns 503 rather than invalid credentials.


### Notification destinations, snapshots and acknowledgement

Queue create/PATCH rejects malformed or non-HTTP(S) webhook URLs with 400;
an empty URL disables future notification snapshots. Each completed job's outbox
row retains its destination, secret and body. Configuration edits apply to future
snapshots; deleting a job does not erase pending deliveries. A malformed legacy
row is counted as a failed attempt and rescheduled independently, so it does not
stop later rows.

"Delivered" means queuelet received a 2xx response before its two-second HTTP
client deadline. A timeout does not reveal whether the receiver completed its
side effect. Failed attempts retry after five seconds; duplicates are possible,
including when the receiver processed a timed-out request. This lesson adds no
attempt cap, dead-letter state, timeout knob or backoff policy for notifications.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""E05 public oracles: verbs in unusual orders.
Public API, the documented lab clock and the event history only; no fixture SQL.
The same probes run against current and historical binaries.
"""
import sys
import probe as p
from probe04 import clock, lease_job

ID = p.ID


def lease_mine(j, w):
    # One lease call: an empty batch is an answer here, not something to wait out.
    batch = p.ok('POST', p.QPATH + '/lease', {'worker_id': w, 'max_jobs': 1})['jobs']
    p.require(not batch or batch[0]['id'] == j, ('leased another job', batch[0]['id'] if batch else None, j))
    return batch[0] if batch else None


def held(v):
    return {k: v[k] for k in ('lease_token', 'leased_by', 'lease_expires_at') if v.get(k)}


def last_event(j):
    return p.ok('GET', f'/v1/jobs/{j}/events')['events'][-1]['event']


def run():
    if ID == 'U24':
        p.queue(max_attempts=2)
        j = p.enqueue()
        attempts = []
        for _ in range(4):
            w = p.worker()
            item = lease_mine(j, w)
            if item is None:
                break
            attempts.append(item['attempt'])
            p.checked('DELETE', f'/v1/workers/{w}')
        rows = [a['outcome'] for a in p.ok('GET', f'/v1/jobs/{j}/attempts')['attempts']]
        state = p.job(j)['state']
        return len(attempts) > 2 or attempts != sorted(set(attempts)), \
            f'max_attempts 2, lease then delete the worker ×4: {len(attempts)} deliveries, attempt {attempts}, history {rows}, now {state}'
    if ID == 'U25':
        p.queue()
        w = p.worker()
        a, c = p.enqueue(), p.enqueue()
        p.require(p.ack(a, lease_job(a, w)['lease_token'], {'ok': True})[0] == 200, 'ack')
        lease_job(c, w)
        p.ok('POST', f'/v1/jobs/{c}/cancel', {})
        left = {f'{p.job(j)["state"]} {j}': held(p.job(j)) for j in (a, c)}
        return any(left.values()), 'lease fields on terminal rows: ' + '; '.join(f'{k} {sorted(v) or "none"}' for k, v in left.items())
    if ID == 'U26':
        clock('set', at='2031-08-01T00:00:00Z')
        try:
            p.queue(lease_seconds=30, max_attempts=5)
            w = p.worker()
            a, c = p.enqueue(), p.enqueue()
            batch = p.ok('POST', p.QPATH + '/lease', {'worker_id': w, 'max_jobs': 2})['jobs']
            p.require(sorted(i['id'] for i in batch) == [a, c], ('first lease', batch))
            clock('advance', seconds=31)
            p.wait(lambda: all(p.job(j)['state'] == 'queued' for j in (a, c)), 6)
            tokens = {i['id']: i['lease_token'] for i in p.ok('POST', p.QPATH + '/lease', {'worker_id': w, 'max_jobs': 2})['jobs']}
            p.require(sorted(tokens) == [a, c], ('second lease', tokens))
            p.require(p.ack(a, tokens[a], {'ok': True})[0] == 200, 'ack after one expiry')
            p.ok('POST', f'/v1/jobs/{c}/cancel', {})
            seen = {'ack': last_event(a), 'cancel': last_event(c)}
            return seen != {'ack': 'succeeded', 'cancel': 'cancelled'}, f'after one lease expiry, ack logged {seen["ack"]}, cancel logged {seen["cancel"]}'
        finally:
            clock('reset')
    if ID == 'A2':
        p.queue(max_attempts=5)
        j = p.enqueue()
        token = lease_job(j, p.worker())['lease_token']
        deleted = p.ok('POST', p.QPATH + '/purge', {})['deleted']
        p.require(p.nack(j, token)[0] == 200, 'nack after purge')
        state = p.job(j)['state']
        return state in ('queued', 'scheduled', 'retry_wait'), f'lease → purge (deleted {deleted}) → nack leaves {state}'
    raise RuntimeError('unknown id ' + ID)


if __name__ == '__main__':
    try:
        present, detail = run(); print(('PRESENT: ' if present else 'ABSENT: ') + ID + ' — ' + detail)
    except Exception as e:
        print('PROBE ERROR: ' + ID + ' — ' + repr(e), file=sys.stderr); sys.exit(2)

# E06-F03 — The sample worker rounds payload numbers: `echo` returns 9007199254740992 for 9007199254740993 and 1.1 for 1.10

Seen at: export of `explore-it/lesson-05` (stack `queuelet-e06`), experiment 06 (relate-it).
Original observation: [E06 notes](../experiments/06-relate-it/notes.md) P4, 15:35:24Z (H-E06-05, predicted from code).
Prior record: D08 (lesson 01) fixed API-side precision and left "client-side qctl/worker numeric loss" as an unprobed
prediction; this is its first observation.

## Minimal reproduction

Actor: acme key; worker-b (sample worker, documented kinds) serves `reports`, which has a webhook to hooksink.
Clock: real.

```sh
source exploration/experiments/06-relate-it/tools/env.sh
k acme-key POST /v1/queues/reports/jobs '{"kind":"echo","priority":9,"payload":{"big":9007199254740993,"dec":1.10}}'
sleep 6
sql "select payload::text, result::text from jobs where id=<id>"
curl -s $QUEUELET_HOOK_URL/admin/records | jq -r '.records[].raw_body'
```
Replay: `tools/p4-journey.sh` (job A).

## Expected (named oracle)

README "Echo returns its payload"; SPEC:63 "Payload values are delivered to workers without loss of numeric
precision". The worker shipped with queuelet (`cmd/worker`, `qctl worker run`) is the documented consumer; echo's
result should be value-equal to the payload. A control job acked by hand with the same numbers (job 311) shows the
API, storage and webhook keep the digits, so the loss is attributable to the worker alone.

## Observed

| Hop | Value of `big` / `dec` |
|---|---|
| request | 9007199254740993 / 1.10 |
| psql `jobs.payload`, `GET /v1/jobs`, lease bytes | 9007199254740993 / 1.10 |
| psql `jobs.result` (after worker-b's echo) | **9007199254740992 / 1.1** |
| outbox body, hooksink raw_body (signature valid) | **9007199254740992 / 1.1** |
| control job 311, manual ack | 9007199254740993 / 1.10 everywhere |

## Variables isolated

- Matters: the job passes through `internal/client.Client.JSON` (`client.go:57`, `json.Unmarshal` without `UseNumber`)
  into `worker.Job.Payload map[string]any` (`worker.go:21`), i.e. float64.
- Does not matter: queue, webhook, priority. Integers ≤ 2^53 and decimals without trailing zeros survive.

## Sibling search

- `worker.go:82, :88` (`sleep`, `fail`) read float64 from the same map — only affects values beyond 2^53, harmless.
- `worker.go:98-110` `http` kind: response decoded with `json.Unmarshal` into `any` → same loss for remote results.
- `cmd/qctl` uses the same pattern for input and output → separate report [E06-F04](E06-F04-qctl-rounds-payload-numbers.md).
- Server side: lease (`jobs.go:81` RawMessage), GET (`store.go` RawMessage), ack (`api.go:53-62` UseNumber), Notify and
  Ship (RawMessage) — exact (P4 control).

## Severity and status

Severity: **low–medium**. Large ids (e.g. 64-bit database keys or snowflake ids) in payloads come back altered from the
reference worker and are notified to partners altered, with a valid signature. Status: **open**.
# E06-F04 — qctl rounds numbers both ways: `enqueue --payload` stores a different number, and `job get` displays one

Seen at: export of `explore-it/lesson-05` (stack `queuelet-e06`), experiment 06 (relate-it).
Original observation: [E06 notes](../experiments/06-relate-it/notes.md) P5, 15:36:13Z (H-E06-14, H-E06-15, predicted
from code; sibling of [E06-F03](E06-F03-sample-worker-echo-loses-precision.md)).

## Minimal reproduction

Actor: acme key; qctl binary from the e06 image (run inside the api container against `http://localhost:8200`).

```sh
source exploration/experiments/06-relate-it/tools/env.sh
q() { docker exec -e QUEUELET_URL=http://localhost:8200 -e QUEUELET_KEY=acme-key queuelet-e06-api-1 qctl "$@"; }
q enqueue reports --kind manual --payload '{"big":9007199254740993,"dec":1.10}'   # {"id": 312, "state": "queued"}
sql "select payload::text from jobs where id=312"     # {"big": 9007199254740992, "dec": 1.1}
k acme-key POST /v1/queues/reports/jobs '{"kind":"manual","payload":{"big":9007199254740993,"dec":1.10}}'   # control, id 313
sql "select payload::text from jobs where id=313"     # {"big": 9007199254740993, "dec": 1.10}
q job get 311      # stored 9007199254740993 / 1.10, printed "big": 9007199254740992, "dec": 1.1
```
Replay: `tools/p5-qctl.sh`.

## Expected (named oracle)

README: "The CLI and the HTTP API expose the same operations." SPEC:63 numeric precision. The same body sent by curl
is stored exactly (job 313), so the CLI must not change the data it sends, and its display must show the stored value.

## Observed

- Input: `qctl enqueue … --payload` stored `9007199254740992` / `1.1` (job 312).
- Output: `qctl job get 311` printed `9007199254740992` / `1.1` for a row whose payload and result hold
  `9007199254740993` / `1.10`.

## Variables isolated

- Matters: `cmd/qctl/main.go:52-57` `jsonOpt` decodes every `--payload`/`--result`/`--json` option into `any`
  (float64) before re-encoding; `main.go:277-280` decodes every response into `any` before `MarshalIndent`.
- Does not matter: endpoint, queue, kind. Values ≤ 2^53 without trailing zeros are unaffected.
- `jsonOpt` also ignores parse errors (an invalid `--payload` becomes `null`) — the API then rejects it (400), so no
  corrupt write results; noted, not counted.

## Sibling search

All qctl verbs share `jsonOpt` and the printer: `ack --result`, `batch --json`, `schedule create --json`,
`queue create/patch --json` (predicted same loss; not probed individually). Worker client: E06-F03.

## Severity and status

Severity: **medium** for the write path (an operator using the documented CLI silently enqueues different data than
typed), **low** for display. One report because one decoding habit causes both. Status: **open**.
# E06-F05 — A result or error containing U+0000 is answered 409 "state_conflict" with driver text; the holder's lease is untouched

Seen at: export of `explore-it/lesson-05` (stack `queuelet-e06`), experiment 06 (relate-it).
Original observation: [E06 notes](../experiments/06-relate-it/notes.md) P6, 15:36:27Z (H-E06-07, predicted from code and
PostgreSQL behaviour). Related prior judgement: E03-H12 / Q-E03-3 (enqueue of `\u0000` → 400 judged a storage limit,
not a bug); this report is about the worker verbs, which E03 did not probe.

## Minimal reproduction

Actor: acme key, my worker 4 (`kinds:["manual"]`). Clock: real. Queue: reports.

```sh
source exploration/experiments/06-relate-it/tools/env.sh
k acme-key POST /v1/queues/reports/jobs '{"kind":"manual","payload":{"case":"ack-nul"}}'      # 314
# lease 314 with worker 4 → token T
k acme-key POST /v1/jobs/314/ack '{"lease_token":"T","result":{"s":"a\u0000b"}}'
#   {"error":{"code":"state_conflict","message":"pq: unsupported Unicode escape sequence"}} [409]
sql "select state,lease_token is not null,attempts from jobs where id=314"   # leased | t | 0
k acme-key POST /v1/jobs/315/nack '{"lease_token":"T2","error":"bad\u0000byte"}'
#   {"error":{"code":"state_conflict","message":"pq: invalid byte sequence for encoding \"UTF8\": 0x00"}} [409]
```
Replay: `tools/p6-nul.sh`.

## Expected (named oracle)

SPEC:16 "A command incompatible with the current state returns 409"; invalid commands are 400 (SPEC:19-22, and the lesson-03 resolution of E03-F04: a storage limit is not a conflict). Here the job *is* leased by the
caller with a valid, unexpired token, so 409 tells the worker "you lost the lease" when the real cause is a value the
store cannot hold. `\u0000` is valid JSON (RFC 8259 §7) and the body passes `decode`. Expected: 400 with a service
message (e.g. `invalid_result` / `invalid_error`), or acceptance with a documented transformation.

## Observed

- ack with `\u0000` in a result string → 409 `state_conflict`, message is the driver's text; job stays `leased`,
  token kept, attempts 0. A retry with a clean result → 200.
- nack with `\u0000` in error text → 409 `state_conflict` with driver text; job stays `leased`. Clean nack → 200, `dead`.
- enqueue payload/kind with `\u0000` → 400 `invalid_job` with driver text (class right, message leaks driver; E03 already
  recorded this).

## Variables isolated

- Matters: U+0000 in a JSON string reaching a `jsonb` (result) or `text` (last_error, attempts.error) column.
- Does not matter: retry flag, queue. A `\u0001` or other control character was not probed.
- Mapping: `ack.go:10-19` and `nack.go` return any database error; `internal/api/jobs.go:88` maps every non-nil error
  to 409.

## Sibling search

- `internal/api/jobs.go:88`: cancel/retry/heartbeat share the same "every error → 409" mapping; a DB outage during
  ack would also read as 409 (H-E04-10, still open).
- Field-level: `heartbeat` takes no strings; `createWorker` name/kinds with NUL → 500 `database_error` (predicted from
  `api/jobs.go:107`, not probed).
- Consequence for the sample worker: an `echo`/`http` result containing U+0000 is acked → 409 → logged as `completed`,
  the job then expires and is retried until `dead` "lease expired" (predicted, not probed).

## Severity and status

Severity: **low–medium**. Wrong error class on the worker protocol hides a data problem as a lease problem; a worker
following the protocol abandons work it still holds, and the job burns attempts by expiry. Status: **open**.
# E06-F06 — A write racing queue deletion is answered 400 invalid_job (enqueue) or 500 database_error (schedule create) with foreign-key driver text instead of 404

Seen at: export of `explore-it/lesson-05` (stack `queuelet-e06`), experiment 06 (relate-it).
Original observations: [E06 notes](../experiments/06-relate-it/notes.md) P9 (15:39:03Z, dead end), P9b (15:39:55Z,
H-E06-10), P9c (15:40:33Z, H-E06-16 sibling, H-E06-17 not hit).

## Minimal reproduction

Actor: acme key. Clock: real. Timing-dependent; reproduced 1/480 enqueues and 5/320 schedule creates.

```sh
source exploration/experiments/06-relate-it/tools/env.sh
ROUNDS=30 bash exploration/experiments/06-relate-it/tools/p9b-race.sh        # enqueue variant
ROUNDS=40 bash exploration/experiments/06-relate-it/tools/p9c-race-siblings.sh  # schedule/batch variant
```
Each round: create queue `e6-race`, issue `DELETE /v1/queues/e6-race`, then 16 enqueues staggered 0–9.9 ms
(P9c: 8 schedule creates + 8 two-job batches); tidy up; repeat.

## Expected (named oracle)

SPEC:15 "A missing resource returns 404" (the queue is gone when the write is applied); SPEC:49-50 no orphans. A
valid command must not be called invalid (400) nor be reported as a server fault (500) with internal constraint names.

## Observed

```text
P9b  delete 26×204, 4×409 | enqueue 64×201, 415×404, 1×400
     {"error":{"code":"invalid_job","message":"pq: insert or update on table \"jobs\" violates foreign key constraint \"jobs_queue_owner\""}}
P9c  delete 39×204, 1×409 | schedule create 8×201, 307×404, 5×500 | batch 8×201, 312×404
     {"error":{"code":"database_error","message":"pq: insert or update on table \"schedules\" violates foreign key constraint \"schedules_queue_owner\""}}
orphan jobs 0, orphan schedules 0 (psql, after both runs)
```
Ownership itself holds: the 002 foreign keys plus the `LOCK TABLE` in deleteQueue never let an orphan in.

## Variables isolated

- Matters: the handler looked the queue up (`queueOrError`, `api.go:240-252`; `createSchedule` `schedules.go:42`) before
  the delete committed, and inserted after (FK check fails). Ordering DELETE first and staggering by a few ms exposes it;
  with simultaneous start (P9) enqueues always won (480×201, 30×409).
- Does not matter: payload, kind. Batch: window present in code but not hit in 320 tries.
- Error mapping: `enqueue.go:87` maps every insertJob error to 400 `invalid_job`; `schedules.go:57` maps to 500.

## Sibling search

`enqueue.go:112-114` batch (400, not observed), `schedules.go:144-165` runSchedule (400 via insertJob — predicted),
`jobs.go:42-50` Lease on a just-deleted queue (`sql: no rows` → 500 — predicted, not probed), `fire.go` (schedule
exists ⇒ queue cannot be deleted; none).

## Severity and status

Severity: **low**. Rare, transient, no data harm; misleads clients into treating a valid request as malformed or a
server fault, and leaks schema names. Status: **open**.
# E06-F07 — Attempt rows (with error text) outlive their job after purge, DELETE and retention; nothing ever removes them

Seen at: export of `explore-it/lesson-05` (stack `queuelet-e06`), experiment 06 (relate-it).
Original observation: [E06 notes](../experiments/06-relate-it/notes.md) P10, 15:41:24Z (H-E06-11, H-E06-18; this is the
charter's "deleting an owner leaves orphans" prediction, confirmed for job → attempt only).

## Minimal reproduction

Actor: acme key, worker 4 (`manual`). Clock: real. Queue `e6-res` (max 2, linear backoff base 0).

```sh
source exploration/experiments/06-relate-it/tools/env.sh
bash exploration/experiments/06-relate-it/tools/p10-residue.sh
```
1. purge: job 885 nacked once ("secret-ish detail", delay 3600 → retry_wait), `POST …/purge` → `{"deleted":1}`.
2. DELETE: job 886 nacked twice → dead; `DELETE /v1/jobs/886` → 204.
3. retention: job 887 acked; PATCH retention_hours 0 → removed by the sweep.

## Expected (named oracle)

Approximation, stated with its bounds. SPEC:122 "Terminal jobs are deleted after `retention_hours`"; SPEC:80-81 attempts
are part of a job's record (`GET /v1/jobs/{id}/attempts`); SPEC:49-50 states the ownership principle "owned … must not
become orphaned" for queues. Read together: when a job is removed, its owned attempt records should go with it (or a
documented retention should apply, as README does explicitly for `job_events`: "retained until lab reset … for
exploration"). The SPEC does not name attempts in the retention rule, so this is a consistency/retention oracle, not a
spec line; the owner may decide otherwise (→ `spec`).

## Observed

```text
GET /v1/jobs/885 and /attempts → job_not_found [404]
psql attempts: 885 | 1 | failed | secret-ish detail
               886 | 1 | failed | fail 1 ; 886 | 2 | failed | fail 2
               887 | 1 | succeeded
orphan_attempts | jobs = 4 | 3    (no attempts table cleanup anywhere in code)
```
Events record `purged`, `deleted`, `retained` (by design). Delivered outbox rows for missing jobs: 3 (SPEC keeps
*pending* deliveries; delivered rows are likewise never removed — sibling).

## Variables isolated

- Matters: any job removal path — `queues.go:170` (purge), `api/jobs.go:32` (DELETE), `expire.go:90-92` (Retain).
- Does not matter: state at removal, outcome kind. Job ids are bigserial and were not reused (887 is a new id for the
  freed idempotency key K1), so the rows are unreachable through the API but never collide.

## Sibling search

- `webhook_outbox`: delivered rows never deleted (no DELETE on the table in code); pending rows must survive (SPEC).
- `workers`: rows for dead incarnations persist (E02 entities) — not job-owned.
- `job_events`: retained by README design (not a defect).
- No FK `attempts.job_id → jobs` (001.sql:7), so the database does not help.

## Severity and status

Severity: **low**. Unbounded growth of `attempts` and indefinite retention of worker error text after the job's
retention period; invisible to API clients. Status: **open** (candidate for `spec` if the owner decides attempts are
history like `job_events`).
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Disclosed E01 findings: immutable black-box oracles for current/historical SUTs.

Only public commands, partner controls, Docker lifecycle and read-only SQL are
used. Unexpected statuses, missing fixtures and failed observations are errors,
not evidence of absence. Run serially: outage/partner cases affect the lab.
"""
import datetime as dt
import json
import os
import pathlib
import subprocess
import sys
import time
import urllib.error
import urllib.request
import uuid
import zoneinfo

ROOT = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
BASE = os.getenv('QUEUELET_URL', 'http://localhost:18200')
HOOK = os.getenv('QUEUELET_HOOK_URL', 'http://localhost:18201')
COMPOSE = ['docker', 'compose', '-f', str(ROOT / 'deploy/compose.yml')]
ID = sys.argv[1]
NAME = 'repro-' + ID.lower() + '-' + uuid.uuid4().hex[:10]
QPATH = '/v1/queues/' + NAME


def call(method, path, body=None, key='acme-key', base=BASE):
    request = urllib.request.Request(base + path,
        None if body is None else json.dumps(body).encode(),
        {'Authorization': 'Bearer ' + key, 'Content-Type': 'application/json'}, method=method)
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(request, timeout=15) as response:
            raw = response.read()
            return response.status, json.loads(raw) if raw else None
    except urllib.error.HTTPError as error:
        raw = error.read()
        return error.code, json.loads(raw) if raw else None


def checked(method, path, body=None, statuses=(200, 201, 204), **kwargs):
    status, value = call(method, path, body, **kwargs)
    require(status in statuses, (method, path, status, value))
    return status, value


def ok(method, path, body=None, **kwargs):
    return checked(method, path, body, **kwargs)[1]


def require(condition, detail):
    if not condition:
        raise RuntimeError(detail)


def sql(query):
    require(query.lstrip().upper().startswith('SELECT '), 'read-only SQL required')
    return subprocess.check_output(COMPOSE + ['exec', '-T', '-e',
        'PGOPTIONS=-c default_transaction_read_only=on', 'postgres', 'psql',
        '-U', 'queuelet', '-d', 'queuelet', '-At', '-v', 'ON_ERROR_STOP=1', '-c', query], text=True, stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL).strip()


def docker(*args):
    subprocess.run(COMPOSE + list(args), check=True, stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL, stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL)


def wait(test, seconds=6):
    deadline = time.monotonic() + seconds
    while time.monotonic() < deadline:
        answer = test()
        if answer:
            return answer
        time.sleep(.12)
    raise RuntimeError('timed out waiting for required observation')


def queue(**kwargs):
    return ok('POST', '/v1/queues', dict(name=NAME, **kwargs))


def enqueue(**kwargs):
    return ok('POST', QPATH + '/jobs', dict({'kind': 'manual', 'payload': {}}, **kwargs))['id']


def worker():
    return ok('POST', '/v1/workers', {'name': NAME, 'kinds': ['manual']})['worker_id']


def lease(w=None, count=1):
    return ok('POST', QPATH + '/lease', {'worker_id': w or worker(), 'max_jobs': count})['jobs']


def job(j):
    return ok('GET', '/v1/jobs/' + str(j))


def ack(j, token, value=None):
    return checked('POST', f'/v1/jobs/{j}/ack', {'lease_token': token, 'result': value}, statuses=(200, 409))


def nack(j, token, **kwargs):
    return checked('POST', f'/v1/jobs/{j}/nack', dict(lease_token=token, error='failure', **kwargs), statuses=(200, 409))


def schedule(**kwargs):
    return ok('POST', '/v1/schedules', dict({'name': NAME, 'queue': NAME, 'kind': 'manual',
        'payload': {}, 'cron': '* * * * *', 'timezone': 'UTC', 'enabled': True}, **kwargs))


def records(j):
    return [r for r in ok('GET', '/admin/records', base=HOOK)['records']
        if isinstance(r['body'], dict) and r['body'].get('job_id') == j]


def stamp(value):
    return dt.datetime.fromisoformat(value.replace('Z', '+00:00'))


def sleep_until(instant):
    while True:
        remaining = (instant - dt.datetime.now(dt.timezone.utc)).total_seconds()
        if remaining <= 0:
            return
        time.sleep(min(remaining, 1))


def present(flag, detail):
    return flag, detail


def ready(path):
    # Restart readiness tolerates transport loss but still requires a live 200.
    # Oracle requests themselves are never converted to absence on failure.
    try:
        return call('GET', path)[0] == 200
    except (urllib.error.URLError, ConnectionError, TimeoutError):
        return False


def recover():
    docker('start', 'postgres')
    wait(lambda: ready('/v1/queues'), 20)
    docker('restart', 'api')
    wait(lambda: ready('/health'), 20)


def run():
    if ID == 'D01':
        p = subprocess.run(COMPOSE + ['exec', '-T', '-e', 'QUEUELET_URL=http://localhost:8200',
            '-e', 'QUEUELET_KEY=acme-key', 'api', 'qctl', 'job', 'get', '999999999999'], capture_output=True, text=True, stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL)
        require('404' in p.stderr, ('CLI did not reach missing-job oracle', p.returncode, p.stderr))
        return present(p.returncode == 0, f'CLI missing-job exit={p.returncode}; stderr={p.stderr.strip()}')
    if ID == 'D02':
        status, _ = checked('DELETE', QPATH, statuses=(204, 404))
        return present(status == 204, f'delete absent queue HTTP {status}')
    if ID in ('D03', 'D18'):
        queue(lease_seconds=1)
    elif ID == 'D20':
        queue(lease_seconds=1, max_attempts=1)
    elif ID in ('D04', 'D17', 'D24', 'U02', 'U03'):
        queue(webhook={'url': 'http://hooksink:8201/hook', 'secret': 'report-secret'})
    else:
        queue()
    if ID == 'D03':
        j = enqueue(); l = lease()[0]
        require(l['id'] == j and l['attempt'] == 1, l)
        wait(lambda: job(j)['state'] != 'leased', 5)
        v = job(j); attempts = ok('GET', f'/v1/jobs/{j}/attempts')['attempts']
        require(v['state'] == 'queued', v)
        return present(v['attempts'] != 1 or len(attempts) != 1,
            f'expired lease counted={v["attempts"]}; attempt rows={len(attempts)}')
    if ID == 'D20':
        # No fabricated attempts: first crash at max_attempts=1 must exhaust.
        j = enqueue(); l = lease()[0]
        require(l['id'] == j and l['attempt'] == 1, l)
        wait(lambda: job(j)['state'] != 'leased', 5)
        v = job(j)
        require(v['state'] in ('queued', 'dead'), v)
        return present(v['state'] != 'dead', f'first crash max_attempts=1 leaves {v["state"]}; completed attempts={v["attempts"]}')
    if ID in ('D04', 'D17', 'D24', 'U02'):
        if ID == 'D04':
            ok('POST', '/admin/mode', {'mode': '500'}, base=HOOK)
        try:
            j = enqueue(); l = lease()[0]
            value = {'text': 'x' * 1500} if ID == 'D17' else {'ok': True, 'n': 4}
            require(ack(j, l['lease_token'], value)[0] == 200, 'valid ack rejected')
            wait(lambda: records(j), 8)
            record = records(j)[0]
            if ID == 'D04':
                observed = wait(lambda: sql(f'SELECT attempts FROM webhook_outbox WHERE job_id={j}') not in ('', '0'))
                delivered = sql(f'SELECT delivered_at IS NOT NULL FROM webhook_outbox WHERE job_id={j}')
                require(record['status'] == 500 and observed, record)
                return present(delivered == 't', f'partner HTTP 500; marked delivered={delivered}')
            if ID == 'D17':
                sent = record['body']['result']
                # Type is U02; decode strings before checking truncation independently.
                if isinstance(sent, str):
                    try: sent = json.loads(sent)
                    except json.JSONDecodeError: pass
                clipped = sent != value
                # Also exercise dead-letter errors independently of result type.
                e = enqueue(); el = lease()[0]; message = 'failure-' + 'z' * 400
                checked('POST', f'/v1/jobs/{e}/nack', {'lease_token': el['lease_token'], 'error': message, 'retry': False})
                wait(lambda: records(e), 8)
                error = records(e)[0]['body']['last_error']
                return present(clipped or error != message, f'result complete={not clipped}; error chars={len(error)}/{len(message)}')
            if ID == 'U02':
                sent = record['body']['result']
                return present(not isinstance(sent, dict) or sent != value,
                    f'result type={type(sent).__name__}; expected object')
            return present(not record['signature_valid'], f'signature_valid={record["signature_valid"]}')
        finally:
            ok('POST', '/admin/mode', {'mode': 'ok'}, base=HOOK)
    if ID == 'D05':
        statuses = [checked('POST', QPATH + '/jobs', {'kind': 'manual', 'payload': {}, 'priority': n}, statuses=(201, 400))[0] for n in (-1, 10)]
        return present(any(s != 400 for s in statuses), f'priority -1/10 statuses={statuses}')
    if ID == 'D06':
        a, _ = checked('POST', QPATH + '/jobs:batch', {'jobs': []}, statuses=(201, 400))
        b, v = checked('POST', QPATH + '/jobs:batch', {'jobs': [{'kind': 'manual', 'payload': {}}] * 501}, statuses=(201, 400))
        count = len(ok('GET', QPATH + '/jobs?limit=500')['jobs'])
        return present(a != 400 or b != 400 or count != 0, f'batch zero={a}, 501={b}, persisted={count}')
    if ID == 'D07':
        statuses = [checked('POST', '/v1/queues', {'name': NAME + suffix}, statuses=(201, 400))[0] for suffix in ('/archive', ' space')]
        return present(any(s != 400 for s in statuses), f'slash/space queue create statuses={statuses}; contract requires rejection')
    if ID == 'D08':
        value = 9007199254740993
        j = enqueue(payload={'id': value}); stored = job(j)['payload']['id']; leased = lease()[0]['payload']['id']
        return present(stored != value or leased != value, f'input={value}; stored={stored}; leased={leased}')
    if ID == 'D09':
        j = enqueue(max_attempts=1); l = lease()[0]
        require(nack(j, l['lease_token'], delay_seconds=3600)[0] == 200, 'valid nack rejected')
        state = job(j)['state']
        require(state in ('dead', 'retry_wait'), state)
        return present(state != 'dead', f'first nack max_attempts=1 leaves {state}')
    if ID == 'D10':
        enqueue(delay_seconds=3600); v = ok('GET', QPATH + '/stats')
        exact = int(sql(f"SELECT count(*) FROM jobs j JOIN queues q ON q.id=j.queue_id WHERE q.name='{NAME}' AND j.state='queued'"))
        return present(v['queued'] != exact, f'stats queued={v["queued"]}; read-only SQL queued={exact}')
    if ID == 'D11':
        v = ok('POST', QPATH + '/jobs:batch', {'jobs': [{'kind': 'manual', 'payload': {}}] * 12})
        ids = v['ids']; w = worker(); first = lease(w)[0]
        require(nack(first['id'], first['lease_token'], delay_seconds=0)[0] == 200, 'release failed')
        wait(lambda: job(first['id'])['state'] == 'queued')
        nextjob = lease(w)[0]
        return present(first['id'] != ids[0] or nextjob['id'] != ids[0],
            f'oldest={ids[0]}, first={first["id"]}, next after public nack/promote={nextjob["id"]}')
    if ID == 'D12':
        delayed = enqueue(delay_seconds=3600); retrying = enqueue(); l = lease()[0]
        require(l['id'] == retrying, l)
        require(nack(retrying, l['lease_token'], delay_seconds=3600)[0] == 200, 'valid nack rejected')
        queued = enqueue(); ok('POST', QPATH + '/purge', {})
        statuses = [checked('GET', f'/v1/jobs/{j}', statuses=(200, 404))[0] for j in (delayed, retrying, queued)]
        return present(any(s != 404 for s in statuses), f'purged scheduled/retry_wait/queued GET statuses={statuses}')
    if ID == 'D13':
        start = time.monotonic(); ok('POST', QPATH + '/pause', {}); s = schedule()
        # Observe two actual minute boundaries; no clock hook or SQL setup writes.
        sleep_until(stamp(s['next_run_at']) + dt.timedelta(seconds=62))
        require(not ok('GET', QPATH + '/jobs')['jobs'], 'pause allowed deliveries')
        ok('POST', QPATH + '/resume', {}); time.sleep(2.2)
        count = len(ok('GET', QPATH + '/jobs')['jobs'])
        advanced = ok('GET', f'/v1/schedules/{s["id"]}')['next_run_at']
        require(advanced and stamp(advanced) > dt.datetime.now(dt.timezone.utc), 'scheduler did not advance during observation')
        ok('DELETE', f'/v1/schedules/{s["id"]}')
        return present(count > 1, f'resume after two missed minute ticks produced={count}; elapsed={time.monotonic()-start:.1f}s; maximum allowed=1')
    if ID == 'D14':
        states = []
        for terminal in ('cancelled', 'succeeded'):
            j = enqueue()
            if terminal == 'cancelled': ok('POST', f'/v1/jobs/{j}/cancel', {})
            else:
                l = lease()[0]; require(l['id'] == j, l); require(ack(j, l['lease_token'])[0] == 200, 'ack failed')
            status, _ = checked('POST', f'/v1/jobs/{j}/retry', {}, statuses=(200, 409))
            states.append((terminal, status, job(j)['state']))
            # If v0 revived it, cancel to isolate the next fixture.
            if status == 200: ok('POST', f'/v1/jobs/{j}/cancel', {})
        return present(any(s != 409 or a != b for a, s, b in states), f'non-dead retry outcomes={states}')
    if ID == 'D15':
        j = enqueue(); s = schedule(enabled=False)
        status, _ = checked('DELETE', QPATH, statuses=(204, 409))
        js = checked('GET', f'/v1/jobs/{j}', statuses=(200, 404))[0]
        ss = checked('GET', f'/v1/schedules/{s["id"]}', statuses=(200, 404))[0]
        require((status, js, ss) in ((204, 200, 200), (409, 200, 200)), (status, js, ss))
        return present(status == 204, f'nonempty owner DELETE={status}; dependent job/schedule={js}/{ss}')
    if ID == 'D16':
        s = schedule(cron='0 0 1 1 *')
        edited = ok('PATCH', f'/v1/schedules/{s["id"]}', {'cron': '* * * * *', 'timezone': 'Asia/Tokyo'})
        disabled = schedule(name=NAME + '-disabled', enabled=False)
        enabled = ok('PATCH', f'/v1/schedules/{disabled["id"]}', {'enabled': True})
        changed = edited['next_run_at'] != s['next_run_at']
        return present(not changed or enabled['next_run_at'] is None,
            f'cron/zone recomputed={changed}; enabling sets next_run_at={enabled["next_run_at"]}')
    if ID == 'D18':
        j = enqueue(); a = lease()[0]
        wait(lambda: job(j)['state'] == 'queued', 5); b = lease()[0]
        old, _ = ack(j, a['lease_token'], {'owner': 'A'})
        current, _ = ack(j, b['lease_token'], {'owner': 'B'})
        return present(old != 409 or current != 200 or job(j)['result'] != {'owner': 'B'},
            f'expired A ack={old}; current B ack={current}; stored result={job(j)["result"]}')
    if ID == 'D19':
        outcomes = []
        # Both token and state are part of F02, with positive control.
        j = enqueue(); l = lease()[0]
        wrong, _ = nack(j, 'wrong-token', delay_seconds=3600)
        outcomes.append(('wrong-token', wrong, job(j)['state']))
        if wrong == 200: ok('POST', f'/v1/jobs/{j}/cancel', {})
        else:
            ok('POST', f'/v1/jobs/{j}/cancel', {})
            late, _ = nack(j, l['lease_token'], delay_seconds=3600)
            outcomes.append(('cancelled', late, job(j)['state']))
        queued = enqueue(); never, _ = nack(queued, 'never-leased', delay_seconds=3600)
        outcomes.append(('queued', never, job(queued)['state']))
        return present(any(status != 409 for _, status, _ in outcomes), f'nack incompatible outcomes={outcomes}')
    if ID == 'D21':
        j = enqueue(); outcomes = []
        for method, suffix, body in [('GET', '', None), ('GET', '/attempts', None), ('POST', '/cancel', {}),
            ('POST', '/retry', {}), ('POST', '/ack', {'lease_token': 'x'}),
            ('POST', '/nack', {'lease_token': 'x', 'retry': False}),
            ('POST', '/heartbeat', {'lease_token': 'x', 'extend_seconds': 1}), ('DELETE', '', None)]:
            status, _ = checked(method, f'/v1/jobs/{j}' + suffix, body, key='globex-key', statuses=(200, 204, 404, 409))
            outcomes.append(status)
        return present(any(s != 404 for s in outcomes), f'foreign namespace get/attempts/cancel/retry/ack/nack/heartbeat/delete={outcomes}')
    if ID in ('D22', 'U04'):
        try:
            docker('stop', 'postgres'); time.sleep(2.2)
            if ID == 'U04':
                auth, _ = checked('GET', '/v1/queues', statuses=(401, 503))
                health, _ = checked('GET', '/health', statuses=(200, 503))
                return present(auth != 503 or health != 503, f'during DB outage auth={auth}; health={health}')
            docker('start', 'postgres')
            wait(lambda: ready('/v1/queues'), 20)
            j = enqueue(delay_seconds=1); time.sleep(4)
            state = job(j)['state']; status, health = checked('GET', '/health', statuses=(200, 503))
            return present(state != 'queued', f'after DB recovery delayed job={state}; health HTTP {status} {health["status"]}')
        finally:
            recover()
    if ID == 'D23':
        now = dt.datetime.now(dt.timezone.utc); zone = zoneinfo.ZoneInfo('America/New_York')
        month = 1 if now.astimezone(zone).utcoffset() == dt.timedelta(hours=-4) else 7
        s = schedule(cron=f'0 2 1 {month} *', timezone='America/New_York')
        local = stamp(s['next_run_at']).astimezone(zone)
        return present(local.hour != 2, f'opposite-season cron requires 02:00 America/New_York; next local fire={local.isoformat()}')
    if ID == 'D25':
        status, v = checked('POST', QPATH + '/lease', {'worker_id': 999999999, 'max_jobs': 1}, statuses=(200, 404))
        require('error' in v, v)
        return present(status != 404, f'unknown-worker error HTTP {status}')
    if ID == 'D26':
        patch, _ = checked('PATCH', QPATH, {'lease_secs': 99}, statuses=(200, 400))
        enqueue(); filtered, _ = checked('GET', QPATH + '/jobs?state=queded', statuses=(200, 400))
        return present(patch != 400 or filtered != 400, f'typo field PATCH={patch}; unknown state GET={filtered}')
    if ID == 'D27':
        s = schedule(); control = schedule(name=NAME + '-control', kind='control')
        ok('PATCH', f'/v1/schedules/{s["id"]}', {'enabled': False})
        sleep_until(stamp(s['next_run_at']) + dt.timedelta(seconds=2.2))
        observed = ok('GET', QPATH + '/jobs')['jobs']
        count = sum(j['kind'] == 'manual' for j in observed)
        require(any(j['kind'] == 'control' for j in observed), 'enabled schedule control did not fire')
        ok('DELETE', f'/v1/schedules/{s["id"]}')
        ok('DELETE', f'/v1/schedules/{control["id"]}')
        return present(count != 0, f'disabled schedule after real minute boundary produced={count}; enabled control fired')
    if ID == 'U01':
        # Use a disabled schedule to isolate validation from background poisoning.
        s = schedule(enabled=False)
        statuses = [checked('PATCH', f'/v1/schedules/{s["id"]}', body, statuses=(200, 400))[0]
            for body in ({'cron': 'bogus'}, {'timezone': 'Mars/Base'})]
        ok('DELETE', f'/v1/schedules/{s["id"]}')
        return present(any(s != 400 for s in statuses), f'invalid cron/zone PATCH statuses={statuses}')
    if ID == 'U03':
        # Remove unrelated outbox work using a fresh API/partner start, never SQL writes.
        # Six public terminal transitions create the observed timeout-row fixture.
        ok('POST', '/admin/mode', {'mode': 'timeout'}, base=HOOK)
        ids = []
        try:
            for _ in range(6):
                j = enqueue(); l = lease()[0]
                require(l['id'] == j and ack(j, l['lease_token'], {})[0] == 200, 'fixture ack failed')
                ids.append(j)
            wait(lambda: any(records(j) for j in ids), 10)
            start = time.monotonic(); delayed = enqueue(delay_seconds=1)
            wait(lambda: job(delayed)['state'] == 'queued', 25)
            slow = time.monotonic() - start
        finally:
            ok('POST', '/admin/mode', {'mode': 'ok'}, base=HOOK)
            # Let the existing serial batch drain before its control.
            time.sleep(2.3)
            wait(lambda: sql('SELECT count(*) FROM webhook_outbox WHERE delivered_at IS NULL') == '0', 20)
        start = time.monotonic(); control = enqueue(delay_seconds=1)
        wait(lambda: job(control)['state'] == 'queued', 6)
        baseline = time.monotonic() - start
        require(baseline <= 5, f'control too slow to support approximation: {baseline:.2f}s')
        return present(slow > 5, f'six-timeout-row promotion={slow:.2f}s; ok-partner control={baseline:.2f}s; warm-lab bound=5s')
    if ID == 'U05':
        # Existing-key and intra-batch duplicates must return original ids; invalid
        # trailing work must roll back new rows without removing existing work.
        original = enqueue(idempotency_key='existing')
        body = {'jobs': [{'kind': 'manual', 'payload': {}, 'idempotency_key': 'existing'},
                         {'kind': 'manual', 'payload': {}, 'idempotency_key': 'new'},
                         {'kind': '', 'payload': {}}]}
        status, _ = checked('POST', QPATH + '/jobs:batch', body, statuses=(400,))
        persisted = ok('GET', QPATH + '/jobs')['jobs']
        broken = [v['id'] for v in persisted] != [original]
        good = ok('POST', QPATH + '/jobs:batch', {'jobs': [
            {'kind': 'manual', 'payload': {}, 'idempotency_key': 'same'},
            {'kind': 'manual', 'payload': {}, 'idempotency_key': 'same'},
            {'kind': 'manual', 'payload': {}, 'idempotency_key': 'existing'}]})['ids']
        require(good[0] == good[1] and good[2] == original, ('idempotency control failed', good))
        return present(broken, f'invalid trailing element HTTP {status}; persisted={len(persisted)} expected=1; duplicate ids preserved')
    if ID == 'U06':
        statuses = []
        for body in ({'max_attempts': 0}, {'retention_hours': -1}, {'lease_seconds': 0}):
            statuses.append(checked('PATCH', QPATH, body, statuses=(200, 400))[0])
            statuses.append(checked('POST', '/v1/queues', dict(name=NAME + uuid.uuid4().hex[:4], **body), statuses=(201, 400))[0])
        return present(any(s != 400 for s in statuses), f'invalid max/retention/lease PATCH/create statuses={statuses}')
    if ID == 'U07':
        status, _ = checked('POST', '/v1/queues', {'name': NAME + '-bad', 'backoff': {'kind': 'zigzag', 'base_seconds': 5}}, statuses=(201, 400))
        return present(status != 400, f'unknown backoff kind create HTTP {status}')
    if ID == 'U08':
        start = time.monotonic(); j = enqueue(run_at='2020-01-01T00:00:00Z')
        age = ok('GET', QPATH + '/stats')['oldest_queued_age']; elapsed = time.monotonic() - start
        require(job(j)['state'] == 'queued', 'fixture not queued')
        return present(age > elapsed + 2, f'new backdated job queued age={age:.3f}s; elapsed+rounding bound={elapsed+2:.3f}s')
    raise RuntimeError('unknown reproduction id ' + ID)


if __name__ == '__main__':
    try:
        defect, detail = run()
        print(('PRESENT: ' if defect else 'ABSENT: ') + ID + ' — ' + detail)
    except Exception as error:
        print('PROBE ERROR: ' + ID + ' — ' + repr(error), file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(2)
name: queuelet
services:
  postgres:
    image: postgres:17-alpine
    environment:
      POSTGRES_USER: queuelet
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: queuelet
      POSTGRES_DB: queuelet
    ports: ["${QUEUELET_PG_PORT:-15433}:5432"]
    healthcheck:
      test: [CMD-SHELL, "pg_isready -U queuelet"]
      interval: 1s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 30
    volumes: ["data:/var/lib/postgresql/data"]
  api:
    build:
      context: ..
      dockerfile: deploy/Dockerfile
    image: queuelet:${QUEUELET_IMAGE_TAG:-local}
    environment:
      DATABASE_URL: postgres://queuelet:queuelet@postgres:5432/queuelet?sslmode=disable
      QUEUELET_TEST_CLOCK: "1"
    ports: ["${QUEUELET_API_PORT:-18200}:8200"]
    depends_on:
      postgres: {condition: service_healthy}
  hooksink:
    image: queuelet:${QUEUELET_IMAGE_TAG:-local}
    command: hooksink
    ports: ["${QUEUELET_HOOK_PORT:-18201}:8201"]
    environment: {WEBHOOK_SECRET: report-secret}
  worker-a:
    image: queuelet:${QUEUELET_IMAGE_TAG:-local}
    command: worker
    restart: on-failure
    environment:
      QUEUELET_URL: http://api:8200
      QUEUELET_KEY: acme-key
      WORKER_NAME: worker-a
      WORKER_QUEUE: emails
    depends_on: [api]
  worker-b:
    image: queuelet:${QUEUELET_IMAGE_TAG:-local}
    command: worker
    restart: on-failure
    environment:
      QUEUELET_URL: http://api:8200
      QUEUELET_KEY: acme-key
      WORKER_NAME: worker-b
      WORKER_QUEUE: reports
    depends_on: [api]
volumes:
  data:
FROM golang:1.26-alpine AS build
WORKDIR /src
COPY go.mod go.sum ./
RUN go mod download
COPY . .
RUN CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -o /out/api ./cmd/api && CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -o /out/worker ./cmd/worker && CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -o /out/qctl ./cmd/qctl && CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -o /out/hooksink ./cmd/hooksink
FROM alpine:3.22
RUN apk add --no-cache ca-certificates tzdata
WORKDIR /app
COPY --from=build /out/ /usr/local/bin/
COPY migrations/ migrations/
CMD ["api"]
